thread:
maria perez: quick API contract q — for the /v1/generate endpoint, when a client sends a param out of allowed range (e.g. temperature = 5), should we return 400 (Bad Request) or 422 (Unprocessable Entity)? also thinking of adding a `retryable` boolean in the error body so clients can logic retry. thoughts?

ajay singh: my read: use 400 for syntactic/shape/validation issues (missing/incorrect types or out-of-range numeric params). 422 works for semantic failures (payload understood but semantically wrong, e.g., incompatible model flags). less important than clear docs, but consistency matters. for retryable: prefer explicit flag in body (or `retry_after`) for transient errors.

sam choi: +1 to ajay. small nit: 400 is what most SDKs expect for client mistakes. 422 historically used by some APIs for validation too, but it's less common. keep 4xx = client, 5xx = server/transient.

lena okafor: +1. also, please avoid overloading 500 for things clients might retry. we had a disk-thrashing incident last month where clients saw 500 and retried aggressively. If the condition is transient (eg overload, degraded pool), return 503 or 429 with `Retry-After`.

maria perez: got it. can we land on a concrete error shape to standardize across endpoints? rough draft: 

```json
{
  "code": "ValidationError",
  "message": "temperature must be between 0 and 2",
  "field_errors": [
    {"field": "temperature", "message": "out of range", "value": 5}
  ],
  "retryable": false
}
```

is that OK? note: keeping `code` machine-friendly helps programmatic handling.

ajay singh: that looks good. couple suggestions: 1) use a short-cased kebab or camel `code` values (e.g., `validation.error` or `validation_error`) so clients can switch on them. 2) include an optional `hint` or `docs_url` for common errors. 3) for rate limits / capacity, prefer 429 + `Retry-After` header and an error `code` like `rate_limit.exceeded`.

sam choi: +1 to a consistent `code` namespace. and for retryability semantics:
- 4xx: retryable=false (except maybe for `rate_limit` where retryable=true)
- 429: retryable=true, include Retry-After header (seconds)
- 5xx (non-idempotent): retryable=false by default, but for known transient server overloads return 503 with `retryable=true` and Retry-After

lena okafor: also remember backward compatibility: adding optional fields (like `field_errors`, `docs_url`, `retryable`) is safe — older clients ignore them. changing status codes is risky. prefer adding new codes before changing codes.

maria perez: noted. ok next: should we include `retryable` at top level or under `meta`? top-level is easier to find. any objections?

ajay singh: top-level ok, keep it boolean. we can later extend to `retry_strategy` if needed.

api-bot: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/api-spec/pull/432 — adds `error_envelope.md` and maps of status->codes. CC @ajay @lena for review.

maria perez: thanks — i'll add an entry to the API contract doc and drop a short migration note for SDKs. can someone do a quick review of the PR this week? @ajay @lena

ajay singh: i'll take a look tomorrow morning.

lena okafor: can review after stand. prefer to land wording about 422 vs 400 explicitly.

maria perez: perfect. if we agree, i'll update the spec and follow up with a tiny release note for SDKs (non-breaking). :thumbsup:

sam choi: sounds good — also can we add a small test case in the compliance suite asserting `retryable` present for rate-limit and absent for validation?

maria perez: yes will add tests. thanks all.

(End of thread)
